task_name: `Home` follows the entrance and keeps the session in every phase

rubric.result: The objective promises four things and each has a line in the diff. (1) 'wires the new form': Home.tsx now passes onOpened={sessionOpened} / onUnreachable={sessionUnreachable} to both StartPlanForm instances, which is exactly the prop pair StartPlanFormProps declares (onOpened: (opened, request) => void, onUnreachable: (request) => void), and planStarted/planStartUncertain/the uncertain-start reconciliation branch are gone as the task's Call-site paragraph orders. (2) 'the coordinating session's state': <CoordinatingSessionStatus /> is rendered, and the component polls GET /coordinating-session every 2 s, so the state appears with no extra callback. (3) 'keeps the terminal on screen and writable in every phase': the <section className="home__sessions"> that holds SessionsPanel + CoordinatingSessionStatus sits at Home.tsx:458, a sibling of the workspace section and outside every currentStage branch, so it renders in request, review and implementation, and nothing disables it. (4) 'reaches the later stages through the restore path it already has': helpers.tsx grows openRestored(), which seeds WorkflowSnapshotStorage and /active-plans, and the nine converted suites reach review/implementation through it instead of pressing the entrance button. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line names it('keeps the coordinating session reachable while a slice is implemented') and fixes the assertion as: Home opened restored in the implementation stage, the terminal's region on screen AND its input not disabled. Home.sessions.test.tsx:104 carries that exact name; the arrange opens Home with /active-plans reporting an implementing plan (the restore path, same end state as openRestored({phase:'implementing'})), and line 108 waits for 'Agente asignado', i.e. the implementation stage. Line 109 asserts screen.getByRole('region', { name: 'Terminal de la sesión' }) — the terminal's region on screen. The second half is measured behaviourally: lastTerminal().onDataHandler?.('ls -la') followed by expect(fetching).toHaveBeenCalledWith(`/sessions/a1/input`, objectContaining({ method: 'POST' })). That is the same property the plan's phrase names — the terminal accepts what is typed — and the literal phrase was not expressible: the on-screen terminal is @xterm/xterm rendering into a div, with no DOM control carrying a disabled attribute to assert toBeDisabled() against. Same input, same stage, same property, measured through production (SessionTerminal.onData -> SessionsClient.type).

The brief carries one block, Call site (frontend/src/pages/home/Home.tsx), with the four lines of the sessions section. Home.tsx:458-461 reproduces it name for name and indentation included: <section className="home__sessions" aria-label="Sesiones en marcha"> with <SessionsPanel /> and <CoordinatingSessionStatus /> inside. No Contract or Current state block accompanies it, so there is no signature, error or constant to compare beyond that. The symbols the wiring touches do line up: the import path 'app/coordinating-session/components/coordinating-session-status' resolves to an existing index.ts, and sessionOpened/sessionUnreachable are assignable to StartPlanFormProps' onOpened/onUnreachable.

Row by row, the rows this diff bears on: D-21 ('no phase of the page may hide it, replace it with a progress panel or disable its input') is implemented exactly — one home__sessions section outside every currentStage branch, holding the panel and the coordinating session's state, with no disabled prop anywhere near it; the task's own verification pins grep -c 'home__sessions' to 1. D-26 ('the entrance keeps its shape ... its one button opens the brainstorming') is honoured: Home keeps rendering the same StartPlanForm with its four fields and now wires it to the open callbacks instead of the start ones. The button-literal row ('Arrancar brainstorming') is respected by every test that presses or queries the button; the literal itself lives in StartPlanForm from task 11. D-13, D-1, D-18, D-25, D-10, D-11, D-16 and D-22 have no line in this frontend diff that bears on them, and none is reopened: no phase is journalised (the snapshot is still reconciled against /active-plans evidence), no cmux name appears, no gate is triggered from code.

Exemplars: SessionsPanel.tsx / useLiveSessions.ts / SessionsMother.ts are the shape this diff imitates — the new wiring is one more component rendered inside the section that already held SessionsPanel, with no new module and no new client. Rules read: CLAUDE.md (identifiers, test names and the amendment prose are English; the only Spanish added is rendered copy — 'No se pudo contactar con el backend' / 'No se pudo abrir el brainstorming. Inténtalo de nuevo.' — which is the exemption CLAUDE.md and style.md both grant), frontend/README.md (absolute imports, named exports, no prose, BEM; the yardstick.test.ts that measures this is inside the green suite) and the frontend-best-practices skill (no semicolons, no export default, no relative import across folders, UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants — all held). architecture.md: the pages layer importing from app/ is the direction already established. boundaries.md and domain.md have no subject: no adapter, port or value object is touched. decisions.md: no business rule is written twice by this diff. defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — the diff NARROWS the Reconciliation union by deleting the 'uncertain-start' member with its branch, and the dispatch over it stays member-by-member with no catch-all; the one new value, brainstormingUnreachable, is a genuine two-state fact about the last open attempt, while the form's richer OpenOutcome vocabulary ('opened' | 'refused' | 'backend-unreachable') stays inside StartPlanForm, so no vocabulary is collapsed into a boolean; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: the new state is a boolean, openRestored builds typed WorkflowSnapshot/ActivePlan values, and the JSON in the suites is wire payload at the fetch boundary; (3) two fields that have to agree, sentinels included — brainstormingUnreachable and reconciliation are independent facts with two different banners, and they cannot both be live (a mutation-blocked form cannot submit, and every submit runs onInteraction, which clears the flag); no empty string or zero stands in for an absence; (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: no error type is added, and the only throw is the test guard 'no terminal was created', named for what happens. Two tensions declared rather than charged, because the task's own **Files:** line makes the compliant move impossible: testing.md asks for a mother ('the objects a test needs are built by a mother') and the frontend skill for Object Mothers from src/__scenarios__/, yet the active-plan fixture is written by hand a third time (Home.sessions.test.tsx:14, beside the copies in implementProgress and implementHistory) because __scenarios__/ is outside this task's Files; and testing.md's 'test helpers hang off their test type ... not in a loose function and not in a shared module' is contradicted by the brief itself, which orders openRestored into the pre-existing shared helpers.tsx. One thing observed and deliberately not charged: sessionOpened's body, setBrainstormingUnreachable(false), can never change anything (StartPlanForm calls onInteraction at the top of every submit, which already clears it), which simplicity.md's 'which call breaks without it?' would answer with none — but the prop is required by the form's contract, so the only alternative is an empty callback, and that is not obviously better.

I read every '-' line of the nine test suites against the brief, because 'the whole frontend suite is green' is satisfied by deletion as easily as by conversion. Seven pre-existing tests leave Home.startPlan.test.tsx and one leaves Home.sessions.test.tsx. Five are authorised by name — 'its uncertain-start tests go with the branch they measured': restore-a-matching-plan-on-retry, block-a-duplicate-start-while-recovery-is-unavailable, keep-the-form-blocked, remain-blocked-on-repeated-recovery and discard-an-uncertain-start all drove the submittedRequest branch of reconcile that the diff deletes. One more is authorised by 'planStarted ... leave[s] with the plan the form no longer starts': 'should show the plan the backend started with a link to its issue' measured planStarted's effect, and what survives of it is still measured — 'Plan arrancado' in Home.restoreWorkflow.test.tsx:85/154/278, the agent in Home.implementProgress.test.tsx:122, the issue link's href in Home.implementPlan.test.tsx:53. The sessions one is a replacement the brief's **Tests:** line names, and it is stricter: instead of the region 'Sesiones en marcha' during implementation it asserts the terminal region inside that same section plus a keystroke reaching POST /sessions/a1/input. Everything else in the other suites is arrange conversion with the assertions kept (baseline red/green, the three layout tests, the navigation trail and right column, planEvents, implementProgress, implementHistory), and two rewrites are stricter, not weaker: Home.baseline gains a findByRole('heading', {name:'Revisar plan'}) before asserting the notice is absent. Two residues remain unaccounted for and are the findings below, both small: the malformed-path refusal case is gone with no sentence asking for it, and one restoreWorkflow test keeps a name whose second half nothing can fail on any more. A third, mentioned and not charged: Home.implementPlan.test.tsx:150 lost expect(fetching).not.toHaveBeenCalled() — 'discarding makes no backend call' — because the stub is now installed after the click.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code, and I traced each assertion back to it. The live question in Home.sessions.test.tsx:133 is rendered by CoordinatingSessionStatus.tsx:25 from what useCoordinatingSession read over GET /coordinating-session — and that component reaches the page only because of this diff's line in Home.tsx. The terminal region and its writability come from SessionTerminal.tsx:71 and its onData -> SessionsClient.type(session.id, text), with the stub sitting at window.fetch, i.e. outside the program. The only double of a module is vi.mock('@xterm/xterm'), a third-party terminal emulator that cannot render in jsdom; the assertion on it (written / onDataHandler) is on what production handed the library, which is testing.md's 'the observable effect: what the port received', not a behaviour living in the fixture. openRestored is arrange only — it writes the snapshot with the real WorkflowSnapshotStorage and answers /active-plans, the same shape Home.restoreWorkflow.test.tsx already used — and no expected value in the diff is hard-coded in place of a production computation.

Inside the declared files, every hunk traces to a sentence. Home.tsx: the section line is the Call-site block, the callback swap and the removal of planStarted/planStartUncertain/'uncertain-start' are the paragraph under it. The new brainstormingUnreachable state and its banner are not gratuitous: StartPlanForm requires onUnreachable, and the pre-existing test 'should say the backend is unreachable when the network fails' — which the brief never says to delete — asserts that banner text, so the wiring the objective asks for has to land somewhere visible. The one added test, 'should clear the unreachable banner once the form is edited again', covers the new line in formInteracted, which is what testing.md's mutation sweep would otherwise leave unwatched. helpers.tsx's openBrainstorming/openRestored are named by the brief. Nothing listed under ### Out of scope is touched: no plugin/skills/brainstorming file, no backend start-plan use case or adapter, no gate or dispatcher, and Home's review and implementation stages are kept working rather than deleted. The plan hunk is an AMENDMENT and it is justified: it adds frontend/src/pages/home/__tests__/Home.restoreWorkflow.test.tsx to this task's **Files:** and explains why — that suite imports pressStart from the shared helpers.tsx, which now clicks 'Arrancar brainstorming', so it could not stay green untouched. I checked what the amendment does NOT do: it removes no route, and it leaves **TDD:**, **Tests:** and the two **Verification:** commands exactly as they were, so no control was disarmed by it.

Three tests are added, all in Home.sessions.test.tsx, and I loaded control-tower-loop:test-driven-development and read its testing-anti-patterns.md reference before looking for anything beyond the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness, no sleep and no network — every request is answered by the stubbed fetch, waitFor replaces every timing guess, and the xterm mock removes the only piece that needs a real canvas. Isolated: each test installs its own stub, afterEach unstubs the globals and setupTests.ts clears localStorage after every test, so openRestored's snapshot cannot leak; MockTerminal.instances is a static that grows, but lastTerminal() only reads .at(-1), which under StrictMode's double mount is the live terminal, and the reload test unmounts and re-stubs before its second half. Verifies real behaviour: the question test would fail the moment <CoordinatingSessionStatus /> left Home, the TDD test asserts a POST that only SessionTerminal's onData can produce, and the replay test can fail for its own reason — if the remount did not resubscribe, the new terminal's written would be empty. On the finer half I found nothing I can pin to the skill's text: no assertion on a '*-mock' element's existence (anti-pattern 1), no test-only method added to production (2), the xterm mock is understood and minimal rather than 'to be safe' (3), the stubbed payloads mirror the real ones the motherss already declare (4), and mock setup is not the bulk of any of the three. The names are not the skill's 'should <action>' shape, but the plan wrote those three names itself in its **TDD:** and **Tests:** lines, so that is not the implementer's to answer for.

findings.what: The malformed-path refusal case was deleted, and no sentence of the task asks for it. The diff overwrites it in place with the not-a-checkout test and then deletes the original copy of that one further down, so the net effect is one refusal case fewer: the suite no longer feeds StartPlanMother.malformedPath() to the form. The brief authorises the uncertain-start tests and says the suite 'points at /coordinating-session'; it says nothing about dropping a refusal case. The weight is small, which is why this is low and not more: the production line it exercised is a single branch (StartPlanForm.tsx:176, {refusal?.kind === 'refused' && <Banner ... title={refusal.error} />}) and two surviving tests still drive it, with CoordinatingSessionMother.oneRepositoryOnly() and StartPlanMother.notACheckout(). Side effect worth noting: StartPlanMother.malformedPath() and planNotStarted() are now exports with no caller in the tree, and __scenarios__/ is outside this task's Files, so they cannot be cleaned up here.

A pre-existing test keeps a name whose second half nothing can fail on any more. Its arrange changed from 'press the button and start a plan' to openRestored({ phase: 'planning' }), so no plan is ever started in it, yet the name still promises 'without starting the plan twice' and the assertion that used to carry that half, expect(fetching).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1), now counts /active-plans calls rather than /start-plan ones — it can only fail if the recovery is asked twice, which is already the subject of 'should request active plans once under StrictMode' at line 160. testing.md's rule for a judge who cannot run anything applies here: 'ask whether that assertion could fail for the reason its name gives, and if it could not, that is the finding'. The fix is one word in the name, not a new assertion: the start half left legitimately with planStarted, which the brief does authorise.
